caption:
Photoroom turns a phone photo of a product into a clean shop listing: it cuts out the background, adds a new one, a shadow and the right size for each marketplace.
The free plan includes 250 exports a month for the core tools. Paid plans start at $7.50 a month, billed yearly.
The full step by step guide is on neurafeedai.com.

site_article.headline: How to use Photoroom for product photos, step by step
site_article.dek: Photoroom cuts your product out of a phone photo, puts it on a clean or AI made background and sizes it for each marketplace. Here is how to do it, what the free plan covers and what the paid plans cost.
site_article.summary: Photoroom is an AI photo editor for product photos that removes backgrounds, generates new scenes, adds shadows and edits whole batches at once. The free plan includes 250 exports a month for the core tools, and paid plans start at $7.50 a month billed yearly.
site_article.seo_title: How to use Photoroom for product photos (free plan explained)
site_article.seo_description: How to use Photoroom for product photos: remove the background, add an AI scene and shadow, edit a batch, and what the free plan and $7.50 Pro plan include.
site_article.answer_summary: Upload a product photo to the Photoroom app or web app, let it remove the background, then add a white or AI generated background and a shadow, resize it for your marketplace and export. The free plan includes 250 exports a month with the core tools; paid plans add AI credits and higher export limits.
site_article.hero_alt: A product photo edited in Photoroom, shown on a new AI generated background.

paragraphs.text: If you want to know how to use Photoroom for product photos, the short version is this: you upload a plain phone photo, Photoroom cuts the product out, and you put it on a clean or AI generated background sized for the place you sell. Photoroom pitches itself as an AI editor for sellers, with tools for background removal, AI backgrounds, shadows, retouching, resizing and batch editing. Its pricing page invites you to start free and pick a plan that fits your product volume.

Photoroom runs as an iPhone app, an iPad app, an Android app, a web app at app.photoroom.com and a Shopify app. There is no separate desktop program listed; on a computer, Photoroom points you to the web app in your browser. Desktop payments go through a credit card, while mobile subscriptions are billed through the App Store or Google Play.
What the Photoroom free plan gives you

According to Photoroom's own product pages, the free plan includes 250 exports a month when you use the Background Remover, Retouch and Templates, with limited access to the AI features. That is enough to test the app on a real shop listing before paying anything. The pricing page does not show a free plan card next to the paid ones, so the free limits are easiest to find on the tool pages.

Paid plans are priced by volume. On the pricing page, with yearly billing, Pro costs $7.50 a month with 8,000 AI credits and 1,000 exports, Max costs $20.99 a month with 25,000 AI credits and 3,000 exports, and Ultra costs $82.50 a month with 75,000 AI credits and 10,000 exports. Photoroom notes that credit amounts can vary by country. All three paid plans include the core tools, AI shadow presets, AI Fill and AI resizing. Video for ads, product pages and the Shopify integration start at Max.

Exports are counted per image, whether you save from the editor, from a batch or through a Shopify sync, and the limits apply to images up to 2K resolution. Photoroom says it sends a warning at 80 percent and 100 percent of your quota; after that, exports pause until the next billing cycle unless you upgrade. eesel, a software company that reviewed the pricing, calls the mix of credits and export limits confusing, so check the meter before a big job.
How to use Photoroom for one product photo

paragraphs.title: 1. Take a simple photo
paragraphs.text: Photoroom does the cutting, but it cannot invent detail that is not in the picture. Shoot the product on a plain surface, in even light, with the whole item in frame and nothing overlapping it. A clean source photo gives a clean edge.

paragraphs.title: 2. Upload it and remove the background
paragraphs.text: Open the app or the web app and upload the photo. Photoroom removes the background automatically and leaves the product on a transparent layer. If you only need a cutout, you can stop here and export it as a transparent image.

paragraphs.title: 3. Choose a background
paragraphs.text: For marketplaces that want a plain look, use a white background. For social posts or your own store, try AI Backgrounds, which builds a styled scene around the product, or upload a background of your own. Make a few versions and keep the one where the product still looks like the real thing.

paragraphs.title: 4. Add a shadow and clean up
paragraphs.text: Add an AI shadow so the product sits on the surface instead of floating. Use Retouch to remove a stray object, a tag or a mark you do not want in the shot.

paragraphs.title: 5. Resize for where you sell
paragraphs.text: Use the templates or AI resize to fit the shape each platform wants, such as a square listing photo or a tall story. Then export. Each saved image counts as one export against your plan.
Keep one plain white version of every product even if you love the AI scene. Marketplaces and customers both trust a plain shot, and it is the fastest one to reuse.
How to edit a whole catalog with batch mode

Batch mode is the reason many sellers pay. Photoroom says it applies the same edits across many images at once, so a full set of product photos can get the same background, shadow and size in one pass. Photoroom's plan cards list separate monthly batch export limits by tier, and the figures differ between its pages, so check the pricing page for the current number before you plan a large job.

paragraphs.title: 6. Set up one photo, then apply it to the rest
paragraphs.text: Get one photo exactly right first: background, shadow, size. Then upload the rest of the set in batch mode and apply the same edits. Look through the results before you export, because one odd photo, such as a reflective item or a busy background, can need a manual fix.

Photoroom is fast for clean, simple products, but it is still guessing at edges. Fine hair, glass, see through packaging and shiny surfaces are where cutouts tend to go wrong, so zoom in before you publish. AI scenes can also make a product look better than it is, and that leads to returns. Use them for mood, and keep at least one honest plain photo in every listing. Finally, the pricing has two meters, AI credits and exports, and the core tools are unlimited only under a fair use policy, so heavy users should read the plan page closely before choosing a tier.

For a small shop with a few dozen products, the free plan is a fair way to test the workflow. If you list new items every week or need video and Shopify sync, the paid tiers are built for that volume.
